subject: ist-pt
title: IST.PT.------WO.EXT.PRI.
description: Closing diagram of vol1, in EXT.F(II)-22. (C)IST-PT (the concept of isolated particulars) is crossed with WO-EXT-PRI (world extension principle — note: not WO-EXP-PRI 'world expansion principle' from the back-of-book glossary, but the diagram-only term 'world *extension* principle'; the difference matters: extension implies productive enlargement rather than mere expansion). The structural pairing closes vol1's argument by asking what isolated particulars contribute to a world-wide extensional principle — i.e., does the work of individual creative musicians (isolated particulars) actually feed world-grade extension? TRS (transition) → IST-PT; DYM-F (dynamic functionalism) → IST-PT; PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) → IST-PT; PR-TRS (primary transition) → IST-PT; INFO-OR (information order) → IST-PT — *five* independent upstream feeds. DYM-F also → ALT-C-PG (alternative composite progressionalism) → MT-IMP (multi-implications). PROG-CONT → WO-EXT-PRI (the crossing partner) → P-FC (particular focus). Structural argument: isolated particulars is a *hub* fed by five independent upstreams (transition, dynamic functionalism, progressional continuance, primary transition, information order). Progressional continuance is the singular feed reaching world extension principle. World extension principle then produces particular focus — meaning the world-extensional principle's productive output *terminates* at particular focus, the very level where vol1 has been working throughout. The diagram is Braxton's closing structural statement: vol1 has spent itself examining the particular focuses of world creativity precisely because particular focus is the terminal output of world-extension itself. The book ends where its terms began — the particular *is* the world-extensional output, not the way to it.
